Upon encountering a new game or world I will iterate over several builds til the first quarter of the game (in my estimation) or when some serious deficit presents itself. Held out on this game but it was on sale. Totally hooked.

Here are notes on my third char in FO4:

  • Str 3 is fine. Just learn what things are optimal to pick up. You never 'miss out' on an item because you didn't collect it, most times you can return or the item respawns. The exceptions will be bobble head and magazines that provide boosts - go ahead and pick those up.

Eg- if you are not Role-Playing a Simian Melee toon, you never need to pick up a bag of concrete.

  • Scouring the entire map is fun but unnecessary to experience a full world they have made a real 'game on rails' experience. To understand my meaning, in the first town of Concord, the buildings not boarded up have lit lanterns by the doors. You can go through the first 10 levels just following bread crumbs - even going into a building through one door, exiting the back door or basement, and end up in the next zone the game devs wanted you in.

I only played to level 15 twice so I don't know everything, but I just got to lvl 10 without ever running out of weight limit by doing the following:

  • only pick up junk with gears, springs, radioactive materials, copper, or things with chips and fiber.

  • every time you use a workbench or station in Sanctuary or whatever 'home base' you set, store all junk like putting on your seatbelt. Once trade routes are established, a global pool of material is enabled, though gear stored in workshops as objects (pre-dismantle) will remain local to their camp. (By object I mean that although the material contained in those objects is available at all settlements, the objects only show up in their respective local workbenches)

  • when you have a mission, quick travel to the nearest 'camp' and store all junk, equip yourself and then go to the mission. When you finish the mission, quick travel back and store all loot again if you need to go back and clean up loose ends.

Don't spend a second over encumbered. There is no reason. It is literally counter productive, quest items have 0 Weight

  • any items that improve combat stats, put on your settlers and equip. (T on PC)

Other stats are irrelevant to the game AFAIK - I boost perception hoping they will see raiders sooner, but at least I know it will do hit modifier.

  • modded armor and weapons apply to 'defensive' settlers.

  • if you put an assortment of weapons and corresponding ammo in a container in a central location in your camps, settlers will go and upgrade if there is a fight. Easy way to 'RP' by providing weapons, without needing to micromanage.

  • looks like establishing camps West to east then moving south and establish camps across the lower parallel and pushing south will keep the game balanced. Eg. If you push south you would be defending from tougher enemies.

  • on defending a base in person - you are the only element that can kill your NPC settlers. If they are disabled and you Pat Tilman them they are off your roster. But they can't friendly fire each other, so hook em' up with frags and set your graphics on Max!

  • on this playthrough I focused on Chr, agl, int so I could sneak/hack/lockpick but also quickly go tier 2 leader so I don't have to forage the wasteland myself
